title: Region assertion operator sandbox and evidence playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sandbox doc for the operator-facing workflow when a tenant requests a region assertion (soft or hard pin). It captures quick-step operator procedures, evidence capture templates, simulation notes from the staging lab, and a small checklist for Canary + rollback conditions. Goal is to create a compact, copyable runbook operators can follow when a customer asks for a region pin or when automated enforcement flags require manual verification.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, On-call operators, Solutions Engineers handling pin validation, and Customer Success for evidence handoff.
- Scope: Hosted + Dedicated + Private (VPC). Focus on assertions that require human review (exceptions, ambiguous residency metadata, KMS location mismatches).

Quick glossary (operator-friendly):
- soft-assertion: tenant preference recorded, routes prefer region but fallback allowed
- hard-pin: strict geographic enforcement, tenant-data must be resident in region X
- evidence bundle: time-windowed telemetry + request traces + storage-region metadata + KMS key location + customer confirmation email

High-level flow (one-liner):
1) Triage flag -> 2) Verify metadata -> 3) Evidence capture -> 4) Apply temporary hold OR proceed to pin -> 5) Post-change verification + audit bundle upload -> 6) Close / escalate.

Operator checklist (for a triage run):
- [ ] Confirm customer tenant id and legal entity (from CRM ticket)
- [ ] Check tenant.region_preference in tenant service (API: GET /tenants/{id}/residency)
  - note: if region field missing, look for last known region in billing metadata and k8s labels
- [ ] Pull last 7 days of routing decision logs (telemetry tag: residency-routing)
- [ ] Snapshot S3/Blob storage region metadata and bucket creation region (if dedicated/private, also node zone tags)
- [ ] Verify KMS key location: kms-key-info --id <key> (confirm primary/secondary regions)
- [ ] If workload runs in Customer VPC, verify VPC peering/egress egress endpoints and region labels
- [ ] If any mismatch -> collect evidence bundle and open PD-RESIDENCY ticket with severity S2

Evidence bundle template (what to collect and attach):
- trace_ids: list of representative request traces showing cross-region hops
- telemetry snapshot: residency-routing logs (last-7d, sample-size 500)
- storage_manifest.txt: bucket_name:region lines for all tenant-owned buckets
- kms_manifest.txt: key_id:primary_region lines
- customer_confirmation.txt: pasted email from customer legal/ops confirming desired pin
- operator_notes.md: short rationale + chosen action + time + operator id

Applying a temporary hold (when to use):
- Use when customer claims a hard pin but telemetry shows transient cross-region routing, or when legal/contract review is pending. Hold semantics:
  - hold_ttl: default 72h (operator can extend with approval)
  - hold_effect: route all new requests into debugging path (no model inference until verified) OR route to fallback regional-compatible model if SLA tolerates
  - mark ticket: PD-RESIDENCY-HOLD

Hard pin execution steps (operator run):
1) Confirm evidence bundle complete and approval from CS/legal (screenshot or signed doc).
2) Plan maintenance window if write-level migration required (notify customer and oncall).
3) Initiate region pinning API with dry-run flag: POST /residency/pin {tenant_id, region, strict: true, dry_run: true}
   - Dry-run returns mismatch summary and L2 impact estimate. Save dry-run report in ticket.
4) If dry-run OK, schedule pin with rollout window and apply.
5) Trigger post-pin verification: run the verification script (tools/residency/verify_pin.sh) collecting same evidence list.
6) Upload verification bundle to audit store and mark ticket resolved.

Fallback orchestration patterns (operator guidance):
- If pin migration fails mid-rollout, automatically revert routing changes and escalate to eng-private-deployments with the failure logs.
- Preferred rollback signal: >5% error-rate increase OR >30s median latency increase for affected routes.

Staging/sandbox exercises (notes from lab runs):
- Simulation 2026-01-18: applied hard pin on tenant-sim-12 with intentionally mis-tagged buckets -> discovered KMS alias mapping bug. Fix: add KMS region alias resolver in orchestration.
- Keep a weekly sandbox slot for 1 operator to rehearse: label: residency-sandbox-weekly

Telemetry and monitoring additions (ops asks):
- Add explicit residency_decision reason codes to routing logs (values: explicit_pin, inferred_from_billing, fallback_region, operator_hold).
- Emit a residency_evidence_hash id when evidence bundle created to link telemetry + bundle in audits.

Audit packaging and retention:
- Audit bundle format: zip containing evidence bundle + operator_notes + ticket_id and MD5 checksum file.
- Retention policy: store bundles 7 years for enterprise contracts flagged as "legal-sensitive", default 2 years otherwise. Coordinate with legal and records.

Risk map (quick):
- Risk: Silent cross-region writes during migration -> Mitigation: pre-migration dry-run + write-block on storage if supported for window.
- Risk: KMS key not available in pinned region -> Mitigation: KMS cross-region key mirrors or rotate plan documented pre-engagement.
- Risk: Customer UX degraded during enforcement -> Mitigation: fallback model variants + customer communication plan.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who signs off on hold extensions beyond 72h? Proposal: CS Director + Legal approval noted in ticket.
- Can we expose a minimal evidence bundle download for customers? (Privacy/PII risk) -> Legal to advise.
- Automation: can we make the dry-run -> apply path a single operator button in Console with pre-checks locked?  (Product/Console follow-up)

Action items (owners):
- Asha: draft the small CLI helper to assemble evidence bundle (due 2026-03-20)
- Evan: add residency_decision reason codes to routing protobufs (due 2026-03-31)
- Marta: coordinate with Legal to confirm retention policy tiers (due 2026-03-24)
- Priya: schedule weekly sandbox slot and add operator rehearsals to ops calendar (due 2026-03-17)

Notes-to-self / informal:
- keep operator flow minimal, avoid >6 steps during high-severity incidents
- this doc is intentionally terse; longer policy lives in confluence: RDW-REGION-4532

References and links:
- Confluence policy draft: RDW-REGION-4532 (linked artifact above)
- Sandbox lab notes: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/residency-simulations (internal repo)
- Jira ticket template: PD-RESIDENCY-TEMPLATE (attach when opening tickets)

Last updated by Asha Patel on 2026-03-10.
